newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere shares mixed on week in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere shares mixed on week in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares were mixed in the week ended on Friday on the Beirut Stock Exchange and dealers said news that the company began to market Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) worth $115-$125 million boosted trading.
A shares rose to $115 from last week's $114 and B shares were unchanged from $117.875.
Weekly turnover in Solidere shares rose to 47,611 shares from last week's 35,549 and value was $5,502,419.255 from $4,079,534.
Dealers said news that Solidere began marketing GDRs worth $115-$125 million for issue on November 26 boosted the volume.

"The volume of shares traded is up this week and this shows good confidence. It is the positive affect on the market of the GDR issue news," Alain Balian, deputy manager at Lebanon Invest finance house, told Reuters.
Balian said the formation on Thursday night of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's cabinet, with many of his supporters remaining in key portfolios, also had a positive impact on the market.
But another dealer said the cabinet's formation had little impact on the shares on Friday. A shares were unchanged from yesterday's $115 and B shares fell slightly to $117.875 from $118.
Market sources had said on Tuesday that Solidere was making an international offering of 10 million GDRs for an issue size of $125 million.
The market sources said each GDR would be worth one tenth of one of Solidere's shares. The price range on the GDRs was $11.5 to $12.5 for an issue price of $115-$125 million, they added.
A Solidere executive questioned by Reuters on the report at the time declined to comment.

The issue is lead managed by Merrill Lynch International, with a selling syndicate formed by ING Barings, Robert Fleming and Co, Paribas Capital Markets and UBS Ltd and roadshows will take place in the United States, Europe and elsewhere, a source said.
Also traded this week on the Beirut Stock Exchange were 1,000 shares of Ciments Libanais on Tuesday at $1.3125, unchanged from October 11 when they were last traded.
There was no trade for the fourth successive week in the three other companies listed on the BSE: Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index rose 0.12 percent on the week to 84.70 and the BLOM stock index also rose 0.33 percent to 988.51.
